rv.q: But it seems frankly lazy to piggyback on an established and popular entertainment property, gussy up its best bits, and make its flaws somehow worse.
Calling this show a mash-up is an understatement: it's more like pouring a few hundredweight of melodies into a cement mixer lorry and adding several tons of rhinestones.
The whole thing is just too nakedly schmaltzy and commercial, and that’s before one considers the interval champagne bar and the post-match merchandise.
But with this cast, those voices, that book, those arrangements and the lack of anything to connect with, Moulin Rouge! falls flatter than some of the notes we hear on stage.
Without that abandon, it's a spectacle that, to me at least, is insufficiently disreputable.
The stage adaptation of Baz Luhrmann’s Moulin Rouge! is a wildly entertaining night at the theatre.

It’s kitsch, joyful hedonism writ large, bursting with sparklers, streamers and technicolour vitality – and powered by a cast who know only too well that you should perform every show as though it could be your last.
It is ostentatious, absurd, and completely ravishing to look at.

This mill grinds – and yes, there is a bit of that, what with the fishnets and satin and rhinestones and bustiers and long legs whipping over each other – exceeding small, delivering its songs mostly bitesize.
But it has a big sticky lollipop where its heart should be, and instead of starlight, only sequins.
It’s not cheap but it’s unforgettable.
At its red velvety heart this show champions life, survival, passion and the all-important love, making for the perfect escapism we all need right about now mon cheri.
In terms of sheer unadulterated fun, Moulin Rouge! The Musical is hard to beat.
When it really lets rip, there is nothing in the West End that can match it.
The leads perform beautifully and it is hard to believe that it is Bogyo's professional debut.
It’s escapism of the highest order, playing to the gallery as it does with little (if any) subtlety.
A fantastically staged musical that’s more about the spectacle than the substance.

cn.t: A dazzling spectacle of excess that delivers eye-popping production design and energetic dance numbers, but critics are divided on whether the frenetic style compensates for a thin central romance and relentless sensory overload.
